subject: Something really slow in the front-end java communication in .73

messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Something really slow in the front-end java communication in .73
parts:
I have been working with someone elses code again on yet-another-cluster.

The first thing I noticed today was calls to rhwatch with noeval=TRUE were taking forever to finish.  When in theory they should be really fast.

The second thing I noticed was rhread of a tiny amount of data with max=2 took like a minute to finish, but it reported the read time as 0.2 seconds.

The third thing I noticed was a call to rhwatch without noeval=TRUE was taking forever to start.  So long that I killed it once, restarted it, ssh'd into a node to check top (don't have access to the webpage), saw nothing was happening, jps'd a couple of things, and then finally the job actually started.

I think there might be something slow going on in the communication to and from the Java process on the front-end, but I haven't really put my finger on it or got any really data.

Thanks,
Jeremiah

messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Re: Something really slow in the front-end java communication in .73
parts:
I will give you an example, but I am still not sure what the interaction is that is causing it:

> hdfs.setwd(path.hadoop)
> hdfs.setwd("Sim_A2_UNClustered/spatial")
> input = "Bend_State_Annual"
> setwd(path.hadoop)
> setwd("scripts_rounds_2013/export_gzip")
> system.time({data = rhread("Bend_State_Annual", type="map", max=10)})
Read 10 objects(13.76 MB) in 12.69 seconds
   user  system elapsed 
  6.082  14.576  91.895 

You can see there is a small disagreement about how long the read takes.  91 is right.

Also, here is a trivial call to rhwatch:

system.time({x = rhwatch(map=expression({}),input=rhfmt("Bend_State_Annual", type="map"),noeval=TRUE)})
   user  system elapsed 
  4.924  15.396  78.061 


I think maybe I am putting my finger on it when I right this email though.  I think the design of Rhipe isn't quite perfect for very large map file directories, because there is no upward limit to the number of directories in a Rhipe map file on the hdfs.

For example, x above from the trivial rhwatch has
nchar(x$lines$rhipe_input_folder[[1]])
[1] 150149

150k characters worth of input files with the start of it is as:
> substr(x$lines$rhipe_input_folder,1,300)
[1] "/pic/projects/iresm/rhadoop/Sim_A2_UNClustered/spatial/Bend_State_Annual/part-r-00097/data,/pic/projects/iresm/rhadoop/Sim_A2_UNClustered/spatial/Bend_State_Annual/part-r-00043/data,/pic/projects/iresm/rhadoop/Sim_A2_UNClustered/spatial/Bend_State_Annual/part-r-00001/data,/pic/projects/iresm/rhadoop"

There are a total of 1654 part-r directories for this map file input.  

Going forward it may be required to think about how to scan this directory the least amount possible.  Also, the design of map files (with the extra) directory versus sequence files seems to contribute to this problem.  With the advent of rhipe file objects it seems conceivable to scan a map file directory exactly once per an R sessions instead of every single time a rhread or rhwatch is done.

Full disclosure: this isn't actually a HDFS.  It is lustre storage on high capacity network fabricate.
